summary: Page conversation listings by sender and literal subject filters without reading the whole mailbox

replay.detail: No claim replay or projection rebuild is required.

schema.detail: Normal startup schema installation adds desired_message_subject_index, a partial index on desired(subject) WHERE kind='message'. Native and legacy sender expression indexes are reused. No database schema identity or checkpoint rules version changes; no new tables, triggers or maintained projections.

rules.detail: Admission, replication, retention and checkpoint rules are unchanged.

compatibility.detail: The native /v1/messages/page endpoint accepts optional from, subject and subject_prefix filters. Subject means the human message title; exact and prefix modes are mutually exclusive, literal and case-sensitive, and require from. The CLI also requires --from with either subject flag. Subject-only filtering is out of scope: avoiding whole-mailbox hydration would require a title index, whose claims-table startup cost is deliberately avoided. Cursors bind normalized sender and recipient, subject mode/text, include_closed and page size, rejecting changed filters. Existing unfiltered cursors remain readable. The CLI retains client-side filtering for older daemons that ignore the new fields; older daemons remain correct but do not gain the speedup. Search and UI behavior are unchanged.

downtime.detail: Existing stores create the small partial desired-message index once during startup, before serving requests. A synthetic database with 3800 messages and 3800 unrelated desired resources took 4.26 ms to create the index; this is a SQLite-only measurement, not a production startup guarantee. Creation scans desired resources, so larger declaration tables can take longer. Subsequent startups reuse the index. No message-table backfill is introduced.

manual.detail: No operator action is required. Upgrade the serving daemon to receive the listing speedup. Within --from ACTOR, use --subject for an exact title or --subject-prefix for a literal prefix. Subject-only filtering and --since are not introduced.

recovery.detail: The additive index contains no authoritative state. Existing message order, lifecycle and recipient-discovery semantics are preserved. Known existing limitation: a legacy root-body send alone is absent from recipient-specific unfiltered listings, so filtered recipient listings also omit it; no-recipient listings can include it. Page cursors remain bounded local creation-order positions, not durable incremental-change watermarks.
